title: Protein Extraction and Western Blot of Human Lung Organoids
author: Morris Baumgardt
materials: From here all steps On ice . Keep tubes, reagents and buffers on ice.

steps.title: Collect Organoids
steps.instruction: Collect organoids from at least two wells of a 24-well plate (approx. 300,000 cells per well, total ~600,000 cells).

substeps.instruction: Remove organoid media by aspiration.
Add 1 mL ice-cold PBS to the organoids.
Transfer organoids on ice to a 15 mL LoBind Tube using a 1000 µL pipette.

steps.title: Extract Protein
steps.instruction: Lyse the organoids and extract protein using RIPA buffer.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 300 x g for 5 minutes at 4 °C.
Add protease inhibitor to the RIPA buffer on ice.
Add 75 µL of RIPA buffer containing protease inhibitor to the pellet.
Break the organoid pellet by repeated resuspension (3 times) using a disposable syringe with a 27G needle.
Transfer the sample to a 1.5 mL LoBind tube.
Centrifuge at 16,000 x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C.
Collect and transfer the supernatant (~ 50 µL) to a 1.5 mL LoBind tube on ice.

steps.title: Quantify and Prepare Protein
steps.instruction: Quantify protein concentration and prepare samples for SDS-PAGE.

substeps.instruction: Use 5 µL of RIPA-lysate in a DC Assay for protein quantification (dilute 1:10 or 1:50 in PBS if required per manufacturer's instructions).
Prepare samples using 50 µg of protein lysate (based on DC assay results) with 4x Laemmli protein sample buffer.
Shake samples at 95 °C for 7 minutes at 1000 rpm.

steps.title: Run SDS-PAGE
steps.instruction: Separate proteins using a Bio Rad 7.5% Mini-Protean TGX Precast Gel (Cat# 456-1023).

substeps.instruction: Arrange gel chambers in the electrophorator and fill the tank and the gel chamber with 1x Running-Buffer; remove the comb carefully.
Load 5 µL Kaleidoscope Protein Standard (Precision Plus Protein Kaleidoscope Prestained Protein Standards #1610375) into lane 1.
Load 50 µg of sample per lane (increase to 100 µg for low expressed proteins).
Run the gel at 100 V for up to 1.5 hours (until the blue front line runs out of the gel).
Once finished, reduce the voltage instead of switching off the power to prevent protein diffusion until blotting is ready.

steps.title: Prepare Blotting Materials
steps.instruction: Prepare the membrane and buffers for protein transfer.

substeps.instruction: Keep the 1x blotting buffer bottle in the freezer for 1.5 hours before use.
Equilibrate the PVDF membrane (0.45 µM methanol for 15 seconds) and transfer it to the 1x blotting buffer.
Soak 2 sponges and 4 filter papers (per gel) in 1x blotting buffer.

steps.title: Transfer Proteins to Membrane
steps.instruction: Transfer proteins from the SDS gel to the PVDF membrane.

substeps.instruction: Equilibrate the gel in 1x blotting buffer for 2 minutes.
Assemble the transfer sandwich in this order: White side of retainer (top), Sponge, 2 filter papers, PVDF Membrane, SDS Gel, 2 filter papers, Sponge, Black side of retainer (bottom).
Remove air bubbles between the gel and membrane using a pipette to squeeze out extra liquid.
Place the sandwich in the transfer apparatus, add ice, and fill with 1x Blotting-Buffer until completely covered.
Transfer at 100 V for 1 hour.

steps.title: Block and Incubate Membrane
steps.instruction: Block the membrane and incubate with antibodies.

substeps.instruction: Wash the membrane with PBS.
Block the membrane in Odyssey blocking solution for 1 hour.
Cut the membrane if multiple protein detection is required.
Add primary antibody (diluted in pure Odyssey blocking solution) and incubate on a shaker overnight at 4 °C.
Wash the membrane three times with 1x PBS-T for 5 minutes each.
Incubate the membrane with secondary antibody solution (in 1x PBS-T with 5% milk) for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash the membrane twice with 1x PBS-T for 5 minutes each, followed by a final wash with 1x PBS for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Detect Proteins
steps.instruction: Visualize proteins using ECL solution and film exposure.

substeps.instruction: Prepare ECL solution and incubate on the membrane according to manufacturer's instructions (2 minutes for Thermo Scientific Kit; 5 minutes for Amersham Kit).
Use the Amersham Kit for ACE2 detection and the Thermo Scientific Kit for all other proteins.
Expose film until an adequate signal is determined for ACE2 (120 kDa), TMPRSS2 (54 and 25 kDa), and FURIN (87 kDa).
